opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Christopher Myers (E012) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, the maximum access is write (admin requires the role to own the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). The requested write level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Christopher Myers (E012) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training max out at read access; admin is never allowed. Requested write is above the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes for E012 conflict on a material fact: HR states Christopher Myers is full-time (which would allow write), while Security states he is a contractor with basic security training (which caps access at read, since write requires advanced training and admin is never allowed for contractors). Given the contradictory employment-type evidence, I grant the most restrictive level that is guaranteed to be within policy. Requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, so the maximum allowed under the restrictive interpretation is read.

- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.
